titulo: Europe’s Digital Wallets May Be More Traceable Than Intended
resumo: Millions of European Union citizens should soon have access to digital wallets , as member states roll out their implementations of the European Digital Identity Regulation ahead of an end of the year deadline. But the digital identity wallets, which are intended to provide a secure and private place to store identifying information such as bank account information, diplomas, and government IDs such as driver’s licenses, could leave behind a trail of cryptographic clues that makes it possible to recognize someone across services. Cryptographers warn that the technology protecting individual privacy may not yet go far enough to stop people from being tracked. Advances in cryptographic techniques since the law was passed in 2024 means this problem could be solved. However, the law doesn’t require that these techniques be used, and cryptographers that IEEE Spectrum spoke with are split as to whether the wallets should be rolled out at all without such a requirement in place, and whether they’ll be secure enough without it. resumo: Direct Storage 1.4 is a Microsoft technology that optimizes the flow of data between the SSD and the graphics card, allowing loading times in games – particularly in open-world titles – to be almost completely eliminated. At the heart of this version is support for the Zstandard codec (Zstd for short), an extremely efficient compression method. Normally, the central processing unit (CPU) has to laboriously decompress game data before it can be displayed. With Direct Storage 1.4, this task shifts directly to the graphics card (GPU), which can perform the decompression much faster using Zstd codecs. With Direct Storage 1.4 technology, the graphics processor handles the decompression. This works quickly thanks to highly efficient compression using Zstd codecs.
